newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila asks Indonesia help on fugitive legislator.
newsitem.headline: Manila asks Indonesia help on fugitive legislator.

text.p: The Philippines on Friday asked Indonesia for help in finding fugitive legislator Romeo Jalosjos, who faces charges of statutory rape of an 11-year old girl, Foreign Affairs Secretary Domingo Siazon said.
"We have been requested by the chairman of the House ethics committee to request the assistance of the Indonesian government and that request was made this morning," Siazon told reporters.

Members of the ethics committee of the House of Representatives unanimously voted on Thursday to recommend the suspension of Jalosjos for 60 days after a 72-hour deadline set by the legislature for him to surrender to the police expired.

Jalosjos, a member of President Fidel Ramos's ruling coalition in the legislature, has evaded arrest since a Manila judge on December 26 issued 14 separate warrants of arrest against him for two counts of statutory rape and 12 acts of lasciviousness.

General Manuel Pepino, head of a police task force in the southern Mindanao region, said on Thursday he had information that Jalosjos left the country on a speedboat from a southern beach resort on December 26 for Indonesia.
"I am 99.9 percent sure about this information my men gathered," Pepino told reporters in southern Zamboanga city.
Siazon said Manila has cancelled the diplomatic passport of Jalosjos early this week.

"His (Jalosjos's) passport is no longer valid. So if the authorities in the country where he is now know that, they will not honour him. He will be arrested and then contact will be made with the Philippine embassy for his deportation," Siazon added.

State prosecutors filed statutory rape charges against Jalosjos after an 11-year-old girl gave a statement saying the legislator had sexual relations with her several times in his Manila apartment last year, paying her amounts ranging up to 10,000 pesos ($385) each time.
The prosecutors said the girl's father brought her to the politician in exchange for money. The father faces a separate charge of exploitation.
President Fidel Ramos last week ordered a manhunt for Jalosjos during mounting media criticism of police failure to locate the lawmaker.
Jalosjos was earlier reported by some newspapers to have gone to Malaysia.
